rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a trace Boron addition to modify interfacial cohesion, while the target paper uses High-Pressure High-Temperature (HPHT) treatment to transform the microstructure. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (compositional vs. processing), so the hypothesis does not reconstruct the paper's intervention.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses a homogenizing solution treatment and room-temperature tensile testing, while the target paper uses HPHT at 6 GPa and 1473 K. The hypothesis conditions (ambient pressure, lower temperature) contradict the paper's high-pressure, high-temperature regime.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis mechanism relies on Boron segregation enhancing interfacial cohesion and delaying microcrack nucleation. The target paper's mechanism involves coherent interfaces enabling dislocation transfer and hierarchical patterns activating multiple deformation mechanisms. These are different classes of mechanisms (interfacial cohesion vs. dislocation transfer and hierarchical deformation).
rationale.outcome_agreement: Both predict simultaneous improvement in strength and ductility, but the hypothesis does not specify the magnitude, while the target paper predicts a doubling to ~1150 MPa and ~36% elongation. The hypothesis captures the right property and direction in general terms only.
